claim: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) stimulates regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation (RRub) on distinct 40S ribosomal proteins.
source: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) or the ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) pathway stimulates regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation (RRub) on distinct 40S ribosomal proteins, yet the cellular role and fate of ubiquitylated proteins remain unclear.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015) and is consistent with established knowledge in the field.

claim: Activation of the ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) pathway stimulates regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation (RRub) on distinct 40S ribosomal proteins.
source: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) or the ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) pathway stimulates regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation (RRub) on distinct 40S ribosomal proteins, yet the cellular role and fate of ubiquitylated proteins remain unclear.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work and established knowledge about RQC pathway function.

claim: uS10 ubiquitylation is dependent upon eS10 ubiquitylation.
source: We demonstrate that uS10 and uS5 ubiquitylation are dependent upon eS10 or uS3 ubiquitylation, respectively, suggesting that a hierarchical relationship exists among RRub events establishing a ubiquitin code on ribosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F where eS10-KI cells show substantially reduced uS10 ubiquitylation.

claim: uS5 ubiquitylation is dependent upon uS3 ubiquitylation.
source: We demonstrate that uS10 and uS5 ubiquitylation are dependent upon eS10 or uS3 ubiquitylation, respectively, suggesting that a hierarchical relationship exists among RRub events establishing a ubiquitin code on ribosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D where uS3-KI cells show complete ablation of uS5 modification.

claim: A hierarchical relationship exists among RRub events establishing a ubiquitin code on ribosomes.
source: We demonstrate that uS10 and uS5 ubiquitylation are dependent upon eS10 or uS3 ubiquitylation, respectively, suggesting that a hierarchical relationship exists among RRub events establishing a ubiquitin code on ribosomes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the dependency relationships observed in the knock-in experiments and represents an interpretation of the data.

claim: Stress dependent RRub events diminish after initial stimuli.
source: We show that stress dependent RRub events diminish after initial stimuli and that demodification by deubiquitylating enzymes contributes to reduced RRub levels during stress recovery.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1 demonstrating time-dependent reduction in RRub levels.

claim: Demodification by deubiquitylating enzymes contributes to reduced RRub levels during stress recovery.
source: We show that stress dependent RRub events diminish after initial stimuli and that demodification by deubiquitylating enzymes contributes to reduced RRub levels during stress recovery.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data showing that RRub levels decrease without corresponding protein degradation, and by experiments with Dub overexpression and knockout.

claim: OTUD3 is a deubiquitylating enzyme that antagonizes ZNF598-mediated 40S ubiquitylation.
source: Utilizing an optical RQC reporter we identify OTUD3 and USP21 as deubiquitylating enzymes that antagonize ZNF598-mediated 40S ubiquitylation and can limit RQC activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the poly(A) stall reporter assay (Figure 3) and immunoblotting showing OTUD3 reduces ZNF598-mediated ubiquitylation (Figure 3E).

claim: USP21 is a deubiquitylating enzyme that antagonizes ZNF598-mediated 40S ubiquitylation.
source: Utilizing an optical RQC reporter we identify OTUD3 and USP21 as deubiquitylating enzymes that antagonize ZNF598-mediated 40S ubiquitylation and can limit RQC activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from the poly(A) stall reporter assay (Figure 3) and immunoblotting showing USP21 reduces ZNF598-mediated ubiquitylation (Figure 3E).

claim: OTUD3 can limit RQC activation.
source: Utilizing an optical RQC reporter we identify OTUD3 and USP21 as deubiquitylating enzymes that antagonize ZNF598-mediated 40S ubiquitylation and can limit RQC activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing OTUD3 overexpression increases poly(A) stall readthrough (Figure 3) and knockout reduces readthrough (Figure 6A).

claim: USP21 can limit RQC activation.
source: Utilizing an optical RQC reporter we identify OTUD3 and USP21 as deubiquitylating enzymes that antagonize ZNF598-mediated 40S ubiquitylation and can limit RQC activation.
evidence: This claim is supported by data showing USP21 overexpression increases poly(A) stall readthrough (Figure 3) and knockout reduces readthrough (Figure 6A).

claim: Cells lacking USP21 have altered RQC activity.
source: Critically, cells lacking USP21 or OTUD3 have altered RQC activity and delayed eS10 deubiquitylation indicating a functional role for deubiquitylating enzymes within the RQC pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 6A showing USP21 knockout cells have reduced poly(A) stall readthrough.

claim: Cells lacking OTUD3 have altered RQC activity.
source: Critically, cells lacking USP21 or OTUD3 have altered RQC activity and delayed eS10 deubiquitylation indicating a functional role for deubiquitylating enzymes within the RQC pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 6A showing OTUD3 knockout cells have reduced poly(A) stall readthrough.

claim: Cells lacking USP21 have delayed eS10 deubiquitylation.
source: Critically, cells lacking USP21 or OTUD3 have altered RQC activity and delayed eS10 deubiquitylation indicating a functional role for deubiquitylating enzymes within the RQC pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 6B showing USP21 knockout cells have sustained eS10 ubiquitylation following UV exposure.

claim: Cells lacking OTUD3 have delayed eS10 deubiquitylation.
source: Critically, cells lacking USP21 or OTUD3 have altered RQC activity and delayed eS10 deubiquitylation indicating a functional role for deubiquitylating enzymes within the RQC pathway.
evidence: This claim is supported by data in Figure 6B showing OTUD3 knockout cells have sustained eS10 ubiquitylation following UV exposure up to 24 hr.

claim: Transcriptional or mRNA processing errors can result in the translation of defective or truncated proteins.
source: A prominent source of proteotoxic stress arises during translation where transcriptional or mRNA processing errors can result in the translation of defective or truncated proteins and lead to the accumulation of toxic nascent protein products (Brandman and Hegde, 2016; Schuller and Green, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Brandman and Hegde, 2016; Schuller and Green, 2018).

claim: Transcriptional or mRNA processing errors lead to the accumulation of toxic nascent protein products.
source: A prominent source of proteotoxic stress arises during translation where transcriptional or mRNA processing errors can result in the translation of defective or truncated proteins and lead to the accumulation of toxic nascent protein products (Brandman and Hegde, 2016; Schuller and Green, 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Brandman and Hegde, 2016; Schuller and Green, 2018).

claim: Failure to remove deleterious proteins can lead to aggregation and contribute to human pathologies including neurodegenerative disorders.
source: Failure to remove these deleterious proteins can lead to aggregation and contribute to human pathologies including a wide range of neurodegenerative disorders (Gestwicki and Garza, 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Gestwicki and Garza, 2012).

claim: ISR activation results in rapid global protein synthesis attenuation.
source: ISR activation results in rapid global protein synthesis attenuation while also stimulating the translation of critical stress response factors, including protein chaperones and ubiquitin ligases, that assist in rebalancing homeostasis (Guan et al., 2017; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Guan et al., 2017; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).

claim: ISR activation stimulates the translation of critical stress response factors, including protein chaperones and ubiquitin ligases.
source: ISR activation results in rapid global protein synthesis attenuation while also stimulating the translation of critical stress response factors, including protein chaperones and ubiquitin ligases, that assist in rebalancing homeostasis (Guan et al., 2017; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Guan et al., 2017; Pakos-Zebrucka et al., 2016).

claim: The ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) pathway identifies elongating ribosomal complexes whose progression is halted due to a defect in the translating mRNA or emerging nascent chain.
source: The ribosome-associated quality control (RQC) pathway is one such quality control system that identifies elongating ribosomal complexes whose progression is halted due to a defect in the translating mRNA or emerging nascent chain (Brandman and Hegde, 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Brandman and Hegde, 2016).

claim: RQC pathway components catalyze the degradation of both the mRNA and nascent polypeptide, followed by ribosome subunit recycling.
source: After the initial recognition event, RQC pathway components catalyze the degradation of both the mRNA and nascent polypeptide, followed by ribosome subunit recycling (Ikeuchi et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Ikeuchi et al., 2018).

claim: Defects within the RQC pathway result in the production of aberrant protein products and an eventual accumulation of protein aggregates.
source: Defects within the RQC pathway result in the production of aberrant protein products and an eventual accumulation of protein aggregates (Choe et al., 2016; Defenouillère et al., 2016; Yonashiro et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Choe et al., 2016; Defenouillère et al., 2016; Yonashiro et al., 2016).

claim: Monoubiquitylation of distinct ribosomal proteins is stimulated in response to ISR activation.
source: Monoubiquitylation, which typically does not target proteins for degradation, of distinct ribosomal proteins is also stimulated in response to ISR activation and conditions that stimulate RQC suggesting that ubiquitylation regulates these pathways beyond protein degradation (Garzia et al., 2017; Higgins et al., 2015; Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Matsuo et al., 2017; Simms et al., 2017; Sugiyama et al., 2019; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work (Garzia et al., 2017; Higgins et al., 2015; Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Matsuo et al., 2017; Simms et al., 2017; Sugiyama et al., 2019; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: Monoubiquitylation of distinct ribosomal proteins is stimulated in response to conditions that stimulate RQC.
source: Monoubiquitylation, which typically does not target proteins for degradation, of distinct ribosomal proteins is also stimulated in response to ISR activation and conditions that stimulate RQC suggesting that ubiquitylation regulates these pathways beyond protein degradation (Garzia et al., 2017; Higgins et al., 2015; Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Matsuo et al., 2017; Simms et al., 2017; Sugiyama et al., 2019; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work (Garzia et al., 2017; Higgins et al., 2015; Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Matsuo et al., 2017; Simms et al., 2017; Sugiyama et al., 2019; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: Regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation (RRub) has emerged as a conserved critical initiating signal during RQC events.
source: Regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation (RRub) has emerged as a conserved critical initiating signal during RQC events (Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Matsuo et al., 2017; Simms et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior work (Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Matsuo et al., 2017; Simms et al., 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: The ubiquitin ligase ZNF598 catalyzes site-specific ubiquitylation of eS10 (RPS10) and uS10 (RPS20) to resolve ribosomes that have stalled during decoding of polyA sequences.
source: In mammals, the ubiquitin ligase ZNF598 catalyzes site-specific ubiquitylation of eS10 (RPS10) and uS10 (RPS20) to resolve ribosomes that have stalled during decoding of polyA sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: Ablation of ZNF598 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences.
source: Ablation of ZNF598 or the ribosomal protein RACK1, as well as conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 or eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: Ablation of the ribosomal protein RACK1 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences.
source: Ablation of ZNF598 or the ribosomal protein RACK1, as well as conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 or eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: Mutation of conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences.
source: Ablation of ZNF598 or the ribosomal protein RACK1, as well as conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 or eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: Mutation of conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences.
source: Ablation of ZNF598 or the ribosomal protein RACK1, as well as conserved ubiquitylated target lysines in uS10 or eS10 results in RQC failure and subsequent readthrough of stall inducing sequences (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: Ribosome collisions are the key initiation signal which recruits critical ubiquitin ligases to facilitate RRub.
source: Current models suggest that ribosome collisions are the key initiation signal which recruits critical ubiquitin ligases to facilitate RRub allowing for subsequent nascent chain ubiquitylation, mRNA degradation, and ribosome recycling (Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Simms et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Ikeuchi et al., 2019; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Simms et al., 2017).

claim: Both uS10 and eS10 ubiquitylation are required for mammalian RQC.
source: The observation that both uS10 and eS10 ubiquitylation are required for mammalian RQC suggest a potential structured order of ubiquitylation events may be needed to specifically mark collided ribosomes.
evidence: This claim is based on inference from prior studies and the authors' own data.

claim: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in mammalian cells triggers RRub events on uS3 (RPS3) and uS5 (RPS2) that do not require ZNF598.
source: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in mammalian cells triggers an additional set of RRub events on uS3 (RPS3) and uS5 (RPS2) that do not require ZNF598 and do not function within the RQC pathway and whose function remains uncharacterized (Higgins et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015).

claim: ISR-stimulated uS3 and uS5 RRub events do not function within the RQC pathway.
source: Activation of the integrated stress response (ISR) in mammalian cells triggers an additional set of RRub events on uS3 (RPS3) and uS5 (RPS2) that do not require ZNF598 and do not function within the RQC pathway and whose function remains uncharacterized (Higgins et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015).

claim: The extent of ISR-stimulated uS3 and uS5 monoubiquitylation diminished upon removal of ISR agonists.
source: Studies in mammalian cells have demonstrated that the extent of ISR-stimulated uS3 and uS5 monoubiquitylation diminished upon removal of ISR agonists (Higgins et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015).

claim: ANS induced ubiquitylation of both eS10 and uS10.
source: Consistent with previous studies, ANS induced ubiquitylation of both eS10 and uS10 (Figure 1A; Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Matsuo et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A and citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz et al., 2018; Matsuo et al., 2017).

claim: eS10 ubiquitylation diminished over time during ANS treatment.
source: While eS10 ubiquitylation diminished and uS10 ubiquitylation persisted over time, there was no discernable reduction in the relative amount of the unmodified form of each protein (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: uS10 ubiquitylation persisted over time during ANS treatment.
source: While eS10 ubiquitylation diminished and uS10 ubiquitylation persisted over time, there was no discernable reduction in the relative amount of the unmodified form of each protein (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: There was no discernable reduction in the relative amount of unmodified eS10 or uS10 during ANS treatment.
source: While eS10 ubiquitylation diminished and uS10 ubiquitylation persisted over time, there was no discernable reduction in the relative amount of the unmodified form of each protein (Figure 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A,B.

claim: No accumulation of unmodified or ubiquitylated eS10 or uS10 was observed with combined treatment of proteasome inhibitors and ANS over 12 hr.
source: Further no accumulation of unmodified or ubiquitylated eS10 or uS10 was observed with combined treatment of proteasome inhibitors and ANS over 12 hr indicating that ribosomal proteins are either not rapidly degraded when ribosome stalling is stimulated, or degradation cannot be detected within the limit of immunoblotting approaches used in these experiments.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Figure 1A.

claim: DTT stimulated uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation which subsequently diminished to pre-treatment levels over time.
source: DTT stimulated uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation which subsequently diminished to pre-treatment levels over time (Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The relative amount of unmodified uS5 and uS3 protein remained stable despite global protein synthesis attenuation.
source: Further, the relative amount of the unmodified protein remained stable despite global protein synthesis attenuation (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: UV exposure stimulates uS5, uS3, eS10 and uS10 regulatory ubiquitylation.
source: To further examine the reversibility and timing of distinct RRub events, we utilized UV-induced ISR activation which stimulates uS5, uS3, eS10 and uS10 regulatory ubiquitylation (Elia et al., 2015; Higgins et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Elia et al., 2015; Higgins et al., 2015).

claim: All observed RRub events diminished over time following UV exposure.
source: All observed RRub events diminished over time further indicating the RRub events are reversible (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation preceded uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation after UV exposure.
source: Interestingly, eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation preceded uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation after UV exposure (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: ISR-stimulated uS5 and uS3 RRub events require eIF2α phosphorylation.
source: Consistent with previous studies demonstrating that ISR-stimulated uS5 and uS3 RRub events require eIF2α phosphorylation, uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation occurred coincidently with eIF2α phosphorylation (Higgins et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Higgins et al., 2015) and experimental data from Figure 1E.

claim: uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation occurred coincidently with eIF2α phosphorylation following UV exposure.
source: Consistent with previous studies demonstrating that ISR-stimulated uS5 and uS3 RRub events require eIF2α phosphorylation, uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation occurred coincidently with eIF2α phosphorylation (Higgins et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data from Figure 1E.

claim: Mutating RRub lysine residues in eS10 K138R/K139R did not result in altered protein stability following ANS treatment.
source: We observed no appreciable change in total protein abundance in the eS10 K138R/K139R knock-in (eS10-KI) and uS10 K4R/K8R knock-in (uS10-KI) cells following ANS treatment (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: Mutating RRub lysine residues in uS10 K4R/K8R did not result in altered protein stability following ANS treatment.
source: We observed no appreciable change in total protein abundance in the eS10 K138R/K139R knock-in (eS10-KI) and uS10 K4R/K8R knock-in (uS10-KI) cells following ANS treatment (Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A,B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1A,B.

claim: The inability to ubiquitylate uS5 K54R/K58R did not change the steady-state abundance or the turnover of uS5.
source: Similarly, the inability to ubiquitylate uS5 K54R/K58R (uS5-KI) and uS3 K214R (uS3-KI) did not change the steady-state abundance or the turnover of uS5 or uS3 (Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The inability to ubiquitylate uS3 K214R did not change the steady-state abundance or the turnover of uS3.
source: Similarly, the inability to ubiquitylate uS5 K54R/K58R (uS5-KI) and uS3 K214R (uS3-KI) did not change the steady-state abundance or the turnover of uS5 or uS3 (Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D and Figure 2—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: eS10-KI cell lines completely lack ANS-induced eS10 ubiquitylation.
source: As expected, eS10-KI cell lines completely lack ANS-induced eS10 ubiquitylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Loss of eS10 ubiquitylation substantially reduces uS10 ubiquitylation.
source: However, loss of eS10 ubiquitylation substantially reduces uS10 ubiquitylation (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F) as compared to control cell lines.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: The inability to ubiquitylate eS10 had a negligible impact on the levels of UV-induced uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation.
source: The inability to ubiquitylate eS10 had a negligible impact on the levels of UV-induced uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1F).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1F.

claim: uS10-KI cells maintained their ability to ubiquitylate eS10, uS5, and uS3 despite the loss of uS10 ubiquitylation.
source: In contrast, uS10-KI cells maintained their ability to ubiquitylate eS10, uS5, and uS3 despite the expected loss of uS10 ubiquitylation (Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2B and Figure 2—figure supplement 1E.

claim: The lack of DTT-induced uS3 ubiquitylation in the uS3-KI cells results in complete ablation of uS5 modification.
source: Similar to the hierarchy of eS10 and uS10, the lack of DTT-induced uS3 ubiquitylation in the uS3-KI cells results in complete ablation of uS5 modification while loss of uS5 ubiquitylation did not effect uS3 DTT-stimulated RRub (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Loss of uS5 ubiquitylation did not effect uS3 DTT-stimulated RRub.
source: Similar to the hierarchy of eS10 and uS10, the lack of DTT-induced uS3 ubiquitylation in the uS3-KI cells results in complete ablation of uS5 modification while loss of uS5 ubiquitylation did not effect uS3 DTT-stimulated RRub (Figure 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2C,D.

claim: Loss of ZNF598 function results in readthrough of poly(A) sequences and a subsequent increase in the ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter.
source: Previous studies demonstrated that loss of ZNF598 function and the resulting decrease in eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation results in readthrough of poly(A) sequences and a subsequent increase in the ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Juszkiewicz and Hegde, 2017; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: Expression of OTUB2, OTUD3, USP10 and UCHL1 did not alter the ChFP:GFP ratio of the control reporter.
source: OTUB2, OTUD3, USP10 and UCHL1 expression did not alter the ChFP:GFP ratio of the control reporter while OTUD1 and USP21 only modestly elevated the ChFP:GFP ratio indicating that the identified Dubs specifically alter the ability of ribosomes to progress through a poly(A)-induced ribosomal stall (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: OTUD1 and USP21 only modestly elevated the ChFP:GFP ratio of the control reporter.
source: OTUB2, OTUD3, USP10 and UCHL1 expression did not alter the ChFP:GFP ratio of the control reporter while OTUD1 and USP21 only modestly elevated the ChFP:GFP ratio indicating that the identified Dubs specifically alter the ability of ribosomes to progress through a poly(A)-induced ribosomal stall (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Expression of inactive OTUD3 or USP21 resulted in a substantial reduction of the ChFP:GFP ratios compared to wild type versions.
source: In contrast, expression of the inactive mutants for the deubiquitylating enzymes USP21, OTUD3, and USP10 resulted in a substantial reduction of the ChFP:GFP ratios compared to wild type versions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Expression of inactive USP10 resulted in a substantial reduction of the ChFP:GFP ratios compared to wild type versions.
source: In contrast, expression of the inactive mutants for the deubiquitylating enzymes USP21, OTUD3, and USP10 resulted in a substantial reduction of the ChFP:GFP ratios compared to wild type versions.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Expression of inactive OTUD3 or USP21 resulted in elevated stall readthrough compared to control transfections.
source: Expression of inactive OTUD3 or USP21 resulted in elevated stall readthrough compared to control transfections indicating a possible alternative role for OTUD3 and USP21 within the RQC pathway that is ZNF598 independent.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Exogenous expression of wild type ZNF598 resulted in decreased ChFP:GFP ratios as compared to control transfections.
source: As expected, exogenous expression of wild type ZNF598 resulted in decreased ChFP:GFP ratios as compared to control transfections (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: USP21 and OTUD3, when co-expressed with ZNF598, resulted in a greater than 2.5 fold increase in the ChFP:GFP poly(A) reporter ratio relative to what was observed when ZNF598 was expressed in isolation.
source: Both USP21 and OTUD3, when co-expressed with ZNF598, resulted in a greater than 2.5 fold increase in the ChFP:GFP poly(A) reporter ratio relative to what was observed when ZNF598 was expressed in isolation (Figure 3D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Cells solely overexpressing ZNF598 displayed a 5-fold increase in the abundance of ubiquitylated eS10 compared to untransfected cells.
source: Immunoblot analysis revealed that cells solely overexpressing ZNF598 displayed a 5-fold increase in the abundance of ubiquitylated eS10 compared to untransfected cells (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Exogenous expression of USP21 substantially reduced the ZNF598-stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation in an activity-dependent manner.
source: Exogenous expression of USP21 substantially reduced the ZNF598-stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation in an activity-dependent manner (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Exogenous expression of OTUD3 substantially reduced the ZNF598-stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation.
source: The same result was observed upon expression of OTUD3 and ZNF598 (Figure 3E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: ZNF598-KO cells displayed elevated ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter.
source: ZNF598-KO cells displayed the expected elevated ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter which was modestly enhanced upon further expression of either Dub (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: Expression of USP21 or OTUD3 in ZNF598-KO cells modestly enhanced the ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter.
source: ZNF598-KO cells displayed the expected elevated ChFP:GFP ratio of the stall reporter which was modestly enhanced upon further expression of either Dub (Figure 4A,B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4A,B.

claim: eS10-KI and uS10-KI cell lines allowed for enhanced readthrough of poly(A)-mediated stall events using the stall reporter FACS assay.
source: Consistent with our previous results, eS10-KI and uS10-KI cell lines allowed for enhanced readthrough of poly(A)-mediated stall events using our stall reporter FACS assay whereas uS3-KI and uS5-KI cell lines did not appreciably alter reporter levels compared to parental cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G and citation to prior work (Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).

claim: uS3-KI and uS5-KI cell lines did not appreciably alter reporter levels compared to parental cells.
source: Consistent with our previous results, eS10-KI and uS10-KI cell lines allowed for enhanced readthrough of poly(A)-mediated stall events using our stall reporter FACS assay whereas uS3-KI and uS5-KI cell lines did not appreciably alter reporter levels compared to parental cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1G; Sundaramoorthy et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1G.

claim: USP21 or OTUD3 overexpression in either eS10-KI or uS10-KI cells resulted in a further enhancement of the ChFP:GFP ratio above the respective transfection controls.
source: USP21 or OTUD3 overexpression in either eS10-KI or uS10-KI cells resulted in a further enhancement of the ChFP:GFP ratio above the respective transfection controls (Figure 4C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Expression of inactive OTUD3 reduced the extent of readthrough compared to wild type in both eS10 and uS10 knock-in cell lines.
source: This enhancement was largely activity-dependent as expression of inactive OTUD3 reduced the extent of readthrough compared to wild type in both eS10 and uS10 knock-in cell lines (Figure 4D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Expression of inactive USP21 resulted in reduced readthrough compared to wild type in uS10-KI cells but not eS10-KI cells.
source: Expression of inactive USP21 resulted in reduced readthrough compared to wild type in uS10-KI cells but not eS10-KI cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The combined loss of uS10 and eS10 RRub events results in a stronger RQC defect than loss of either uS10 or eS10 ubiquitylation events alone.
source: These results indicate that OTUD3 and USP21 can demodify both uS10 and eS10, consistent with our immunoblotting data (Figure 3E). Further, these results indicate that the combined loss of uS10 and eS10 RRub events results in a stronger RQC defect than loss of either uS10 or eS10 ubiquitylation events alone.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing enhanced readthrough in knock-in cells with Dub overexpression.

claim: ZNF598 expression stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation in parental HCT116 cells.
source: As expected, ZNF598 expression stimulated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation in parental HCT116 cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: ZNF598 expression in uS10-KI cells failed to induce uS10 ubiquitylation without impacting the ability of ZNF598 to ubiquitylate eS10.
source: ZNF598 expression in uS10-KI cells failed to induce uS10 ubiquitylation without impacting the ability of ZNF598 to ubiquitylate eS10.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: ZNF598 expression failed to ubiquitylate eS10 in eS10-KI cells, and uS10 ubiquitylation was substantially reduced compared to ZNF598 expression in parental cells.
source: Conversely, ZNF598 expression failed to ubiquitylate eS10 in eS10-KI cells, and uS10 ubiquitylation was substantially reduced compared to ZNF598 expression in parental cells.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Expression of wild type USP21 or OTUD3 reduced the abundance of both monoubiquitylated eS10 and uS10 in parental HCT116 cells.
source: While expression of wild type USP21 or OTUD3 reduced the abundance of both monoubiquitylated eS10 and uS10 in parental HCT116 cells, expression of the inactive variants restored ubiquitylation to steady-state levels (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Expression of inactive USP21 or OTUD3 variants restored ubiquitylation to steady-state levels.
source: While expression of wild type USP21 or OTUD3 reduced the abundance of both monoubiquitylated eS10 and uS10 in parental HCT116 cells, expression of the inactive variants restored ubiquitylation to steady-state levels (Figure 4E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: ZNF598 protein levels are 19-fold in excess of OTUD3.
source: Examination of quantitative proteomic datasets from human cell lines revealed that ZNF598 protein levels are 19-fold in excess of OTUD3 while USP21 levels were undetectable indicating that ZNF598 protein levels are in vast excess of either RRub Dub at steady state (Itzhak et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Itzhak et al., 2016).

claim: USP21 levels were undetectable in quantitative proteomic datasets from human cell lines.
source: Examination of quantitative proteomic datasets from human cell lines revealed that ZNF598 protein levels are 19-fold in excess of OTUD3 while USP21 levels were undetectable indicating that ZNF598 protein levels are in vast excess of either RRub Dub at steady state (Itzhak et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Itzhak et al., 2016).

claim: Expression of the poly(A)-reporter with increasing concentrations of exogenous ZNF598 in isolation did not result in a dose-dependent decrease in the ChFP:GFP ratio.
source: Expression of the poly(A)-reporter with increasing concentrations of exogenous ZNF598 in isolation did not result in a dose-dependent decrease in the ChFP:GFP ratio suggesting that ZNF598 expression at the lowest levels tested were sufficient to fully restore RQC function and that elevated ZNF598 levels do not further enhance ribosome stall resolution (Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D.

claim: When equal amounts of USP21 or OTUD3 and ZNF598 expression plasmids were transfected, a substantial increase in the ChFP:GFP ratio was observed as compared to ZNF598 expressed alone.
source: When equal amounts of USP21 or OTUD3 and ZNF598 expression plasmids were transfected, a substantial increase in the ChFP:GFP ratio was observed as compared to ZNF598 expressed alone which further verified the direct antagonism observed previously (Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D.

claim: The reporter ChFP:GFP ratio declined as ZNF598 plasmid transfections were doubled and tripled with respect to USP21 or OTUD3 plasmid DNA.
source: The reporter ChFP:GFP ratio declined as ZNF598 plasmid transfections were doubled and tripled with respect to USP21 or OTUD3 plasmid DNA (Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F,G and Figure 3—figure supplement 2C,D.

claim: Doubling and tripling the expression of USP21 while holding ZNF598 expression levels constant revealed additional readthrough of the poly(A) stall-inducing sequence with increasing ChFP:GFP ratios.
source: Conversely, doubling and tripling the expression of USP21 while holding ZNF598 expression levels constant revealed additional readthrough of the poly(A) stall-inducing sequence with increasing ChFP:GFP ratios, suggesting further antagonism of the ligase.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: In cells overexpressing exogenous wild type USP21, the amount of detectable eS10 ubiquitylation rapidly declined 1 hr post UV exposure.
source: Interestingly, in cells overexpressing exogenous wild type USP21, the amount of detectable eS10 ubiquitylation rapidly declined 1 hr post UV exposure, while uS10 ubiquitylation was completely ablated (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: In cells overexpressing exogenous wild type USP21, uS10 ubiquitylation was completely ablated following UV exposure.
source: Interestingly, in cells overexpressing exogenous wild type USP21, the amount of detectable eS10 ubiquitylation rapidly declined 1 hr post UV exposure, while uS10 ubiquitylation was completely ablated (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: The dynamics of eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation following UV treatment in cells expressing inactive USP21 were unaltered compared to cells without Dox-treatment.
source: Immunoblots confirmed that the dynamics of eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation following UV treatment in cells expressing inactive USP21 were unaltered compared to cells without Dox-treatment. (Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: OTUD3 expression resulted in substantially reduced eS10 ubiquitylation and complete ablation of uS10 ubiquitylation following UV treatment compared to uninduced cells.
source: Similar to what was observed upon USP21 expression, OTUD3 expression resulted in substantially reduced eS10 ubiquitylation and complete ablation of uS10 ubiquitylation following UV treatment compared to uninduced cells (Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5C and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Induction of inactive OTUD3 did not alter either eS10 or uS10 ubiquitylation upon UV treatment.
source: This reduction in eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation was activity dependent as induction of inactive OTUD3 did not alter either eS10 or uS10 ubiquitylation upon UV treatment (Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5D and Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Two separate knockout clones for both USP21 and OTUD3 displayed reduced poly(A)-mediated stall readthrough.
source: Two separate knockout clones for both USP21 and OTUD3 displayed reduced poly(A)-mediated stall readthrough which is consistent with our demonstration that overexpression of OTUD3 or USP21 enhances stall readthrough (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Combined loss of USP21 and OTUD3 did not further reduce stall readthrough compared to individual knockouts.
source: Combined loss of USP21 and OTUD3 did not further reduce stall readthrough compared to individual knockouts suggesting that the Dubs may be acting at distinct points within the RQC pathway (Figure 6A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6A.

claim: eS10 ubiquitylation was rapidly induced following UV exposure and was fully demodified to pre-exposure levels by 16 hr in parental 293T cells.
source: Consistent with previous results, eS10 ubiquitylation was rapidly induced following UV exposure and was fully demodified to pre-exposure levels by 16 hr in parental 293T cells (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: USP21 or OTUD3 knockout cells displayed reduced demodification kinetics following UV exposure with eS10 ubiquitylation persisting up to 24 hr in OTUD3 knockout cells.
source: USP21 or OTUD3 knockout cells displayed reduced demodification kinetics following UV exposure with eS10 ubiquitylation persisting up to 24 hr in OTUD3 knockout cells (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: OTUD3 and USP21 double knockout cells displayed sustained eS10 ubiquitylation following UV exposure compared to parental controls.
source: OTUD3 and USP21 double knockout cells also displayed sustained eS10 ubiquitylation following UV exposure compared to parental controls (Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: USP21 expression reduced both HTN and DTT-induced uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation in an activity-dependent manner.
source: Interestingly, USP21 expression reduced both HTN and DTT-induced uS5 and uS3 ubiquitylation in an activity-dependent manner (Figure 7A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: OTUD3 expression reduced uS5 ubiquitylation, albeit to a lesser extent than UPS21 expression, and had no impact on HTN or DTT-induced uS3 ubiquitylation.
source: However, OTUD3 expression reduced uS5 ubiquitylation, albeit to a lesser extent than UPS21 expression, and had no impact on HTN or DTT-induced uS3 ubiquitylation (Figure 7B).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: Both OTUD3 and USP21 are present in the ribosome pellet fraction.
source: Importantly, both OTUD3 and USP21 are present in the ribosome pellet fraction suggesting that OTUD3 and USP21 associates with ribosomes.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C,D.

claim: OTUD3 is present in 40S containing fractions and largely absent from 80S and polysome containing fractions.
source: Subsequent immunoblotting of gradient fractions revealed OTUD3 to be present in 40S containing fractions and largely absent from 80S and polysome containing fractions (Figure 7E).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: OTUD3 may preferentially demodify ubiquitylated 40S proteins that arise after subunit splitting.
source: These results suggest that OTUD3 may preferentially demodify ubiquitylated 40S proteins that arise after subunit splitting and position OTUD3-mediated deubiquitylation as a putative late step during RQC events.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing OTUD3 localization to 40S fractions.

claim: RRub events are reversible and mediated by deubiquitylating enzymes following activation of the ISR or RQC pathways.
source: Here, we establish that regulatory ribosomal ubiquitylation events are reversible and mediated by deubiquitylating enzymes following activation of the ISR or RQC pathways.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript showing time-dependent reduction in RRub levels and the effects of Dub overexpression and knockout.

claim: USP21 and OTUD3 can directly antagonize ZNF598-mediated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation events.
source: We demonstrate that USP21 and OTUD3 can directly antagonize ZNF598-mediated eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation events.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3E and Figure 4E.

claim: USP21 and OTUD3 expression results in augmented removal of ubiquitin from eS10 and uS10 following UV-induced RQC.
source: Further, we show that USP21 and OTUD3 expression results in augmented removal of ubiquitin from eS10 and uS10 following UV-induced RQC.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5.

claim: USP21 expression represses ISR-stimulated uS3 and uS5 ubiquitylation.
source: USP21 expression also represses ISR-stimulated uS3 and uS5 ubiquitylation.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Expression of OTUD3 results in enhanced stall readthrough compared to knock-in cell lines engineered to lack either eS10 or uS10 RRub sites.
source: Expression of OTUD3 results in enhanced stall readthrough compared to knock-in cell lines engineered to lack either eS10 or uS10 RRub sites indicating that combinatorial ribosomal ubiquitylation is required for optimal RQC function.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4C,D.

claim: Combinatorial ribosomal ubiquitylation is required for optimal RQC function.
source: Expression of OTUD3 results in enhanced stall readthrough compared to knock-in cell lines engineered to lack either eS10 or uS10 RRub sites indicating that combinatorial ribosomal ubiquitylation is required for optimal RQC function.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that combined loss of eS10 and uS10 ubiquitylation results in stronger RQC defects.

claim: RRub represents a combinational post-translational code that imparts distinct functional outcomes on ribosomes.
source: Taken together, our results establish that RRub events are reversible by deubiquitylating enzymes and that RRub represents a combinational post-translational code that imparts distinct functional outcomes on ribosomes.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the hierarchical relationships observed among RRub events and their distinct functional roles.
